newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Boral to review gas distribution structure.
newsitem.headline: Boral to review gas distribution structure.

text.p: Building materials and energy group Boral Ltd said on Wednesday it had initiated a review of the structure of its natural gas distribution holdings.

Boral said the review would have regard for the national competition policy reforms to the natural gas distribution business in Australia, which would require the segregation of the existing business into distinct gas transportation and gas retailing businesses.

Boral said the objectives of the review were to establish a ring-fenced entity owning the natural gas distribution assets which could further invest in energy infrastructure assets as deregulation of the sector proceeds.

"This review demonstrates Boral's firm commitment to our fast growing energy group and gives us a real opportunity to strengthen the company's position through participating in the changes being brought about by deregulation," Boral managing director Tony Berg said in a statement.
"Boral will play a major role in the restructured industry. Although plans have not been finalised, any decision will be predicated on adding value for shareholders," Berg said.

Boral owns and operates gas distribution businesses in Adelaide, Brisbane, Gladstone, Rockhampton, Mt Gambier, Whyalla, Port Pirie, Alice Springs and other regional centres in South Australia and Queensland.
Boral said it would issue a statement to the stock exchange when plans have been finalised.
In 1995/96 ended June 30, Boral Energy, which employs 2,300 people, achieved sales revenue of over A$830 million and made a profit before interest and tax of A$152 million.

From its own reserve base of 870 petajoules and through a wide range of supply agreements with other producers, Boral Energy supplies 132 petajoules equivalent per year of natural gas, LPG, crude oil and condensate to customers throughout Australia and the Pacific.
Boral shares were five cents firmer at A$3.84 at 3.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) on Wednesday.
